result.title: Focus on What You Need: Global-to-Local Dynamic Attention for Multimodal Sarcasm Detection
result.summary: Multimodal sarcasm detection has attracted increasing attention due to the widespread use of images and text on social media platforms. Existing studies generally treat the semantic or emotional inconsistency between images and text as a key cue for identifying sarcastic expressions. However, images in real-world scenarios often contain multiple visual objects, many of which are irrelevant to sarcasm-related semantics. Such redundant visual information may introduce noise during cross-modal interaction, distracting models from focusing on critical sarcasm cues and potentially leading to inaccurate predictions. To address this issue, we propose GLDA (Global-to-Local Dynamic Attention), a multimodal sarcasm detection framework that models cross-modal interactions from a global-to-local perspective. Specifically, GLDA first employs a global multimodal fusion module to capture high-level semantic interactions between visual and textual modalities, enabling the model to identify coarse-grained cross-modal inconsistencies. To further reduce the influence of irrelevant objects, GLDA introduces a local gated cross-modal attention mechanism that dynamically filters redundant visual and textual features and refines multimodal representations at a finer granularity. In addition, a multi-branch learning objective is designed to jointly optimize unimodal and multimodal representations. Experimental results demonstrate that GLDA effectively improves sarcasm detection performance and achieves competitive results compared with existing approaches. The code will be available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/GLDA-DBE6.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 GLDA 框架，先做全局多模态融合捕捉图文粗粒度不一致，再用局部门控跨模态注意力动态过滤冗余视觉与文本特征，并用多分支目标联合优化单模态与多模态表示，用于多模态讽刺检测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其门控跨模态注意力对无关视觉对象的动态筛选与精化，可能与 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、冗余视觉导致的信息坍缩问题相关，可供核查；但论文面向任务判别，不涉及 latent 推理状态的生成与使用。
